claims.claim: Le Guin characterises genre writers of her early period as deliberately cultivating an attempt to be styleless, which she treats as a fault rather than a model.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, interviewed by John Wray, The Paris Review, Art of Fiction No. 221 (2013)
claims.quote: genre writers deliberately cultivated an attempt to be styleless
claims.page: answer on The Wave in the Mind sentence

claims.claim: Le Guin says that when she creates another world with a society on it she tries to hint at the complexity of that society instead of just referring to an empire.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, interviewed by John Wray, The Paris Review, Art of Fiction No. 221 (2013)
claims.quote: I try to hint at the complexity of the society I’m creating
claims.page: opening answers, on the social sciences

claims.claim: Le Guin tells a world-building questioner that event requires location and that where we are affects who we are.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'Navigating the Ocean of Story: Session 1, Continued' (Book View Cafe, 2015)
claims.quote: Event requires location. Where we are affects who we are
claims.page: answer to Marion, on world building

claims.claim: Le Guin prescribes passages that describe what the world looks like, smells like and sounds like as the relief that paces an idea-crammed story.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'Navigating the Ocean of Story - Session 1, Part 5' (Book View Cafe, 2015)
claims.quote: describe what the world looks like, smells like, sounds like
claims.page: answer on stories too crammed with ideas

claims.claim: Adam Roberts writes that the Earthsea books take care to render their world as a believable, lived-in space.
claims.source: Adam Roberts, "Ursula Le Guin, 'A Wizard of Earthsea' (1968)", Adam's Notebook (Medium), 5 February 2023

claims.claim: Adam Roberts characterises the detail in Earthsea as anthropological as much as mythographic, and linguistic as much as geographical.
Adam Roberts observes that Le Guin has a fondness for low walls as boundaries.
claims.quote: Le Guin has a fondness for low walls as boundaries
claims.page: paragraph on the realm of the dead

claims.claim: Richard D. Erlich judges that Le Guin's style has become more colloquial and lower-flown, comparing the language of Tehanu with that of the earlier Earthsea trilogy.
claims.source: Richard D. Erlich, Coyote's Song: The Teaching Stories of Ursula K. Le Guin, Conclusion (SFRA, (c)2000)
claims.quote: Her style has gotten more colloquial, lower-flown
claims.page: Conclusion, section on what has changed

claims.claim: Le Guin, in her Response to the 1975 Le Guin issue of Science-Fiction Studies as quoted by Erlich, said the ideas of the Earthsea trilogy are less detachable from the sounds, rests and rhythms than those of her other work of that time.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, "Response", Science-Fiction Studies (1975), p. 45, quoted in Richard D. Erlich, Coyote's Song, Conclusion ((c)2000)
claims.quote: less detachable from the sounds, rests, and rhythms

claims.claim: Richard D. Erlich credits Le Guin's 1961 story 'An die Musik' with a genius for handling complex issues in a lucid, simple style at the very beginning of her career.
claims.source: Richard D. Erlich, Coyote's Song, Early Works ((c)2000)
claims.quote: a genius for handling complex issues in a lucid, simple style
claims.page: Early Works, section on 'An die Musik'

claims.claim: Le Guin writes that adjectives and adverbs are rich and good and nourishing, and cause obesity in prose only when used lazily or overused.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Steering the Craft, quoted in Nicole Bianchi, '3 Powerful Writing Exercises from Steering the Craft' (2021)
claims.quote: They cause obesity in prose only when used lazily or overused
claims.page: section 2, Practice Eliminating Unnecessary Adjectives and Adverbs

claims.claim: Le Guin advises that when the quality an adverb indicates can be put in the verb itself, or an adjective's quality in the noun itself, the prose will be cleaner, more intense and more vivid.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Steering the Craft, quoted in Nicole Bianchi (2021)
claims.quote: the prose will be cleaner, more intense, more vivid

claims.claim: Le Guin names Somehow a super-weasel, a word that betrays that the author did not want to bother thinking out the story.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Steering the Craft, quoted in Nicole Bianchi (2021)

claims.claim: Le Guin's exercise asks for a paragraph to a page of 200-350 words of descriptive narrative prose written without adjectives or adverbs, using only verbs, nouns, pronouns and articles.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Steering the Craft, exercise quoted in Nicole Bianchi (2021)
claims.quote: (200-350 words) of descriptive narrative prose without adjectives

claims.claim: Michael Swanwick lists archaicisms, false feeling, fake grammar and journalistic prose as the ways Le Guin says language should not be used in fantasy.
claims.source: Michael Swanwick, 'Revisiting Poughkeepsie, Part 2: The Language of the Night', Flogging Babel, 14 October 2010
claims.quote: Archaicisms, false feeling, fake grammar, journalistic prose

verdicts.trueWording: genre writers deliberately cultivated an attempt to be styleless
verdicts.note: Raw Wayback capture of the Paris Review interview. Quote appears word for word in her answer about The Wave in the Mind sentence; the 'fault not model' limb is carried by the same exchange, where she says sf could be 'embarrassingly badly written' and that older men 'prided themselves' on refusing style while 'to me the style is the book'.

verdicts.trueWording: I try to hint at the complexity of the society I'm creating
verdicts.note: Same raw capture. Quote is verbatim (curly apostrophe) in the early answer on drawing on the social sciences; the full sentence also carries the 'another planet, another world, with a society on it' and 'instead of just referring to an empire' limbs.

verdicts.trueWording: Event requires location. Where we are affects who we are
verdicts.note: Verified on the Wayback raw capture (20250416080121id_) of the ursulakleguin.com page, NOT the live host: ursulakleguin.com/robots.txt disallows user-agents 'anthropic-ai' and 'ClaudeBot' from '/', so the live URL was not fetched. Quote verbatim in the reply to Marion, whose question is explicitly about world building.

verdicts.trueWording: describe what the world looks like, smells like, sounds like
verdicts.note: The ursulakleguin.com URL has no Wayback capture and the live host blocks Anthropic agents in robots.txt, so verified on the original Book View Cafe post the claim's own source field names: Wayback raw capture 20151029022249id_ of bookviewcafe.com/blog/2015/10/05/navigating-the-ocean-of-story-session-1-part-5/. Quote verbatim in the reply to Tamara, whose readers called her drafts 'too crammed with ideas'; the surrounding sentence supplies the 'easier pace' and 'moments of relief' limbs.

Medium returned 403 to a direct fetch; verified on the Wayback raw capture 20250908044316id_. Sentence reads that the Earthsea books are careful to render their world as a believable, lived-in space, in the paragraph beginning 'There is a seriousness'. Byline Adam Roberts, Feb 5 2023, confirmed on the capture.

verdicts.trueWording: as mythographic, as much linguistic as geographical
verdicts.note: Same Wayback capture. Page reads 'the attention to detail, as much anthropological (...) as mythographic, as much linguistic as geographical'. The claim's quote fragment 'as much anthropological' is verbatim; the anthropological/mythographic pairing is split by a parenthesis on the page, so the contiguous run quoted here is the tail of it. Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Le Guin has a fondness for low walls as boundaries
verdicts.note: Same Wayback capture. Appears verbatim as a parenthetical in the passage on the realm of the dead, separated from the living by a low wall.

verdicts.trueWording: Her style has gotten more colloquial, lower-flown
verdicts.note: Raw Wayback capture of sfra.org/Coyote/conclusion.htm. Quote verbatim; the same sentence supplies the Tehanu-versus-Earthsea-trilogy comparison limb explicitly.

verdicts.trueWording: than in some of her other, arguably less artful work
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim on the raw Coyote's Song Conclusion capture, and the attribution limbs check out: Erlich writes 'In responding to the 1975 Le Guin issue of Science-Fiction Studies', cites page 45, and the page elsewhere names Le Guin's 'Response' 45. Only the comparison class is over-specified by the claim.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the comparison class 'her other work of that time' — the page sets the Earthsea trilogy against 'some of her other, arguably less artful work', a quality criterion, with no temporal qualifier

verdicts.trueWording: a genius for handling complex issues in a lucid, simple style
verdicts.note: Raw Wayback capture of sfra.org/Coyote/earlyworks.htm; quote is verbatim across a line wrap. Page reads it as the third of four reasons the story matters, 'for showing at the beginning of her career'. The 1961 date and first-published-story status are both on the page under the heading 'An die Musik' (1961).

verdicts.trueWording: They cause obesity in prose only when used lazily or overused
verdicts.note: Raw fetch of nicolebianchi.com. Quote verbatim in the block quotation under heading '2. Practice Eliminating Unnecessary Adjectives and Adverbs'; the preceding clause supplies 'rich and good and nourishing'.

verdicts.trueWording: the prose will be cleaner, more intense, more vivid
verdicts.note: Same block quotation. Both antecedent limbs are on the page: quality of the adverb put in the verb itself (they ran quickly = they raced) and of the adjective in the noun itself (a growling voice = a growl).
Same block quotation. Page continues 'a word that betrays that the author didn't want to bother thinking out the story' — the claim's 'did not' is its own paraphrase, not part of the quoted fragment.

verdicts.trueWording: (200-350 words) of descriptive narrative prose without adjectives
verdicts.note: Raw fetch of nicolebianchi.com, exercise block in section 2. Word-for-word match; the page uses an en dash in 200-350 where the claim uses a hyphen. Page continues 'or adverbs' and 'using only verbs, nouns, pronouns, and articles', so every limb of the claim is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Archaicisms, false feeling, fake grammar, journalistic prose
verdicts.note: Raw fetch of floggingbabel.blogspot.com. Quote verbatim in the paragraph beginning 'Accompanying her discussion', introduced as 'examples of ways it should not' be used. Byline Michael Swanwick and date Thursday, October 14, 2010 both confirmed on the page, as is the title 'Revisiting Poughkeepsie, Part 2: The Language of the Night'.
